original_method: Preserve baseline logs, run one unambiguous approved VM worker count and memory allocation with continuous memory/swap/OOM/ECC/thermal/power monitoring, capture full output/status and stop through a managed abort path.
manual_activity: Engineer resolves exact stress profile and safety limits; qualified operator owns stop/recovery; agent may run only the approved monitored workload.

Require continuous monitoring and a tested stop mechanism before load
Stop on OOM/swap storm, ECC, thermal/power threshold, crash/watchdog, monitoring loss or instability

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source supplies both short `-m 15` and long `--vm 9` forms for the same VM stressor count, so the actual worker count is ambiguous and cannot be safely inferred.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The package, exact command and safety policy can be supplied; static review is complete and this pending execution decision does not block later cases.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row39 Wistron-Memory-00022-V003: choose the authoritative stress-ng VM worker count because `-m 15` conflicts with `--vm 9`; approve package/version/checksum, exact aggregate/per-worker `--vm-bytes 90%` semantics and8-hour command, swap/OOM/ECC/thermal/power/watchdog/responsiveness thresholds, monitoring cadence, baseline-log preservation replacing `dmesg -c`, managed stop, cleanup/recovery and invalid-run policy; DeepSeek's8/80%/300s substitute must not count.

review_improvement: Preserves the intended high-load duration and memory target while isolating the unsafe worker ambiguity and destructive evidence handling.
independent_technical_reasoning: `-m` is the short form of the VM stressor selector, so providing it together with `--vm` using different values does not describe two independent workloads. Worker count also changes how `--vm-bytes` is distributed and can radically alter aggregate pressure. Executing either value without approval could cause an unintended OOM/swap storm and would make the run irreproducible.
